test_title: SSC CGL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 2 March 2023)
subject: general
question: A circle touches all four sides of a quadrilateral ABCD. If AB = 18 cm, BC = 21 cm and AD = 15 cm, then length CD is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any quadrilateral circumscribing a circle, the sum of opposite sides is equal.

Property: AB + CD = BC + AD

18 + CD = 21 + 15

CD = 36 − 18 = 18 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of side AB = 18 cm

Length of side BC = 21 cm

Length of side AD = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a tangential quadrilateral (a quadrilateral that circumscribes a circle), the sum of the lengths of opposite sides is equal: AB + CD = BC + AD.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6d09b2e72e89c84c8afbefe87359b37424ec578b0c08bc59712b35469686ae9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ AB + CD = BC + AD

⇒ 18 + CD = 21 + 15

⇒ 18 + CD = 36

⇒ CD = 36 − 18

⇒ CD = 18 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pitot Theorem

The theorem states that for a tangential quadrilateral, the sum of the lengths of opposite sides is equal. This is derived from the property that tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.

Area of Tangential Quadrilateral

The area of a tangential quadrilateral can be calculated as Area = s × r, where s is the semi-perimeter (s = (a+b+c+d)/2) and r is the radius of the incircle.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A cyclic quadrilateral is one where all vertices lie on a circle. In such cases, the sum of opposite angles is 180° (supplementary angles).</p
